title: Neutral Intermediary
definition: A person or organization that facilitates communication and collaboration between different parties without favoring one side over the other.

difficulty_levels.beginner: Imagine a referee in a sporting event. They don't play the game, but they make sure the rules are followed and the game is fair for all players.
difficulty_levels.intermediate: A neutral intermediary acts as a trustee, steward, or fiduciary, managing resources for a community without personal profit. This role is crucial in decentralized systems to foster collaboration and coordination.
difficulty_levels.expert: The role of a neutral intermediary in decentralized systems is critical for fostering collaboration and coordination. It can take the form of a mediator, arbiter, or escrow agent, ensuring fairness and transparency. In legal and corporate contexts, a neutral intermediary is a trustee or fiduciary, legally obligated to act in the best interests of all parties involved. The challenge lies in creating such a role in decentralized systems without centralizing control or creating incentives for capture.

extra_fields.insight: The need for a neutral intermediary in decentralized systems to foster collaboration and coordination without creating centralized control or incentives for capture.
